annotations.text:
Direction A, “Kitchen table” (built out above): warm paper, Bricolage Grotesque + Figtree, one orange for “needs you”, teal for “decided”.
Static mockups, not clickable. Provider logos on the sign-in screen are placeholders.

Flow: 1 Sign in from an invite link → 2 Home shows what needs your vote and every event in flight → 3 A trip groups its decisions in order, with a running “decided so far” → 4 Vote in round 2 of 3 (shortlist, pick up to 2) → 5 Round 2 closes and the final opens by itself; the organizer can reopen or just call it → 6 The shareable summary that goes back to Messenger.
7 is the sheet for starting a new decision and choosing how many rounds.

Two other directions, sketched low-fi on the trip screen only. B “Scoreboard”: dark, game-like, big tallies and a countdown; makes voting feel like sport, risks feeling competitive inside a family. C “Postcard”: editorial travel journal, serif, photo-led; beautiful for trips, weaker for Friday dinner. Say the word and I will build either out.

Open decision from the brief: these screens assume everyone signs in with Google, Apple or Facebook (the founder’s words). The brief argues voters should instead tap their own name from a roster with no sign-in, because Messenger’s in-app browser breaks OAuth, and only organizers sign in. Choosing that changes 1 Sign in, 3 Trip and 4 Vote, and adds an event-landing roster screen.
